statements.statement: The PLOS One Editors have retracted the article Detecting phishing websites using machine learning technique, because it was one of a series of submissions with concerns about peer review integrity and potential manipulation.
The editors say these concerns call into question the validity and provenance of the reported results, which include the LSTM detector's accuracy of 97.4% on Phishtank and 96.8% on Crawler.
The author either did not respond to the editors or could not be reached.

In Section 3, the draft names Dutta [14] as main evidence, RNN-LSTM URL detector LURL, and cites [14] for accuracy 97.4% and 96.8%, higher than both comparison detectors; the stored paper reports those accuracies.
On the strength of these results the draft chose an LSTM over the two alternatives, and decided not to run a separate model-selection study before the pilot.

In Section 4, the draft starts from the LURL settings by Dutta [14]: two LSTM layers, hidden size 650, learning rate 1.0 with decay 0.73, and does not plan to tune them so results can be read against the published ones.
The PLOS One Editors have retracted the article because it was one of a series of submissions with concerns about peer review integrity and potential manipulation of the publication process.
The editors say these concerns call into question the validity and provenance of the reported results.
Those results are the accuracy results Section 3 relies on and the published results Section 4 settings are read against, so all three uses are touched and the effect on the draft is high.

The PLOS One Editors have retracted the article because of concerns about peer review integrity and potential manipulation, and the editors say these concerns call into question the validity and provenance of the reported results.

In Section 3, the draft names Dutta [14] as main evidence, cites [14] for accuracy 97.4% and 96.8%, higher than both comparison detectors; on that basis decided not to run a separate model-selection study.
In Section 4, the draft starts from the LURL settings reported by Dutta [14] and does not plan to tune them before the pilot, so results can be read against the published ones.
